findings.reason: The protected SQL solution finds missing customer IDs from 1 to MAX(customer_id) using a WITH RECURSIVE candidate_ids CTE. It generates integers 1 through MAX(customer_id), performs a LEFT JOIN against Customers, filters for Customers.customer_id IS NULL (anti-join), and orders by candidate_ids.ids ASC. The query runs in O((m + c) log c) upper bound time and O(m + c) space; no candidate is required.
Recursive CTE generates all integers from 1 up to MAX(customer_id). LEFT JOIN with IS NULL filter correctly extracts only missing IDs in the bounded domain.

Generating m candidates takes O(m) time. Anti-join against c rows takes O((m + c) log c) time upper bound with O(m + c) auxiliary space for recursive table and join buffers. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts Customers table, returning single column ids containing missing integers in [1, max(customer_id)] sorted ascending.

The approach accurately details bounded recursive candidate ID generation, anti-join NULL filtering, ascending ID ordering, and O((m + c) log c) time / O(m + c) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover static numbers table joins, correlated count per candidate overhead, window function gap boundary limits, missing ID 1 handling, consecutive ID empty results, multi-value gap handling, upper bound cap, and numerical sorting priority.

App SQL and native SQL solutions both execute the identical WITH RECURSIVE CTE anti-join query with SHA-256 digest e619110895db202592c2cdfdb8a5be818ddaf3988b8128f99ae852fdd183b0fb. Verified submission remains untouched.

Statement structure and factual evidence confirmed Customers table interface, three examples, two constraints, and 3 local tables. Bound to content SHA-256 f664f3fcf4447d4c2472c9e017471858bb4799b05c7420a91fd1e917f71df270.
